replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: To solve a second order algebraic equation, first bring all terms to one side to set the equation to zero. To find stationary points, take the first derivative of the function f(x) to get f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Then, use the second derivative test or analyze the first derivative’s sign changes to classify them as maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
